title: Best data source? Yahoo vs Alpaca
author: TheColdGhost
selftext:
Good morning! I have been creating a model/platform with Chatgpt Astra where I can backtest and do paper trading. Super cool and nice. That said, I hit limits with yahoo finance. Is Alpaca the best option to obtain data?

I find that the biggest hurdle is in the data collection side. Once that is solved, I can use AI to create algos and do backtesting.

Any help/suggestions are greatly appreciated!

Thanks,

comments.author: TheFertileSloth
comments.body: Depends on your needs and strategies. My primary is massive with a backup of alpaca. Are you leveraging yfinance properly? Doing batches? Etc. You are probably already aware, but if you ever deploy to cloud or anything yfinance pretty much blocks all of those.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Worth knowing before you commit to it: Alpaca's free data tier is IEX only, and IEX is a low single digit share of US consolidated volume. The bars are real, but they are built from a thin slice of the tape, so the high and low on a quiet name can differ from what actually printed. The full consolidated feed sits behind their paid tier.

On daily bars that matters much less. Intraday it will quietly move your fills. Which of the two are you backtesting on?

replies.author: strat-run
replies.body: Alpaca free historic data can be requested as IEX or SIP. The IEX limit is real time.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: That matches the feed parameter in the docs, with the catch that free SIP historical holds back the most recent 15 minutes, so it is fine for backtests and not for anything reading the current bar. Are you pulling free SIP for daily bars, or paying for the realtime side?

replies.author: strat-run
replies.body:
For OP, they only want daily bars so I think they can use the free tier for everything. I don't understand why anyone messes with Yahoo at this point, it was shut down in 2017 and it's all weird scraping hacks to try and make working clients.

If you need real time data then between IEX and the symbol count limits the free Alpaca tier might not work, it doesn't for me.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Daily bars on the free tier work, with one thing worth knowing: the free feed is IEX only, and that applies to the historical bars too. Volume runs well under the consolidated tape and the open and close are IEX prints, not the official ones. For a daily backtest that is usually tolerable. Have you compared the two closes on a few names?

replies.author: strat-run
replies.body:
Free Alpaca historic bars has both the IEX and SIP versions available. For daily bars and highly liquid symbols they aren't that different.

I usually use 1 min bars and the difference is pretty noticeable. It's not bad on the most liquid symbols during market hours but you quickly start seeing data gaps where there was no IEX bar at all.

Not much reason to use historic IEX unless you are trying to understand the problems with using realtime IEX data.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
The gaps hurt a backtest more than the price differences do. A missing minute gets forward filled or dropped, and either way anything keyed to bar count fires at the wrong time.

When you build features, do you drop the gapped minutes or fill them from the SIP set?

replies.author: strat-run
replies.body: Bad bot, at least make sensible questions.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: That last question didn't follow, you'd just pull SIP and skip the gaps. Your daily bars point stands, the free tier covers what OP needs.

comments.author: TheColdGhost
comments.body:
Thanks for the reply. My model is not focused on intraday. The minimum size of data I need is daily data. I was looking at Alpaca’s pro tier at $99 USD, which is not bad. I think that might be the best option?

Another option would be collecting data on a daily basis from yfinance - if that’s even a possibility. Probably need to focus on S&P500 / Nasdaq 100 so the pool is not massive.

Any thoughts are appreciated.

Thanks again.

replies.author: strat-run
replies.body: You can get that for free with Alpaca.

comments.body: Im used databento and switched to tickstream later because of prices on databento. Support and community on tickstream is crazy nice 👍🏼

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The comment about yfinance blocking cloud deployments is the thing that bites everyone eventually, so plan for that before you build anything serious on it. Alpaca is fine for paper trading and basic bars, but the free tier data is IEX-only which means thin volume and weird prints on small caps, so your backtest fills will lie to you. If you're doing anything intraday, the data source matters more than the algo, garbage bars in means garbage signals out. Also be careful with the AI-generated-algo workflow, backtesting on adjusted close while ignoring survivorship bias and delisted tickers is how you get a model that looks amazing and dies live. Batch your yfinance calls and cache aggressively, and treat the whole thing as a data engineering project first, strategy second.
